name: Ordered payload-free diagnostics
purpose: Own the deterministic diagnostic precedence and the construction of ordered, stable, payload-free code sequences.
responsibilities: Declare the single diagnostic precedence order over the Result enum, from handle failures down through context, time, action, permit, quota, and capacity failures.
Build an ordered Diagnostic (code sequence plus at most one bounded numeric locator) from the first applicable failure, highest precedence first.
Guarantee the diagnostic carries no string payload, item, observation, or free-form content, and that the same input yields the same code sequence across runs and builds.
Support bounded multi-failure accumulation for precedence tests while capping the sequence length.
state_ownership: None. The diagnostic is an immutable value produced from inputs; the precedence order is a constexpr table.
interfaces: Diagnostic: codes() const -> bounded code sequence; locator() const -> std::optional<std::uint32_t>
compare(Result a, Result b) constexpr -> std::strong_ordering for deterministic ordering
concurrency: Not applicable; diagnostics are immutable values with no shared state.
errors: No runtime errors; structural static checks assert that Diagnostic holds only enumerable codes and a numeric locator.
deployment: Header-only within the standalone candidate; used by the manager and by tests that assert exact ordered code sequences.
rationale: Isolating precedence in one component makes the stable, ordered, payload-free diagnostic contract (SR-016) a single auditable rule instead of ad-hoc ordering spread across the manager.
